spec.name: Earnings drift v13
spec.notes: Searched 189 variants of this signal; the figure quoted is the best of them and should be read with that in mind. The family has a long record as a premium.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.78 to 1.76 (change -0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.78 to 1.78. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.78 (as submitted, 10 bps: 1.78); it breaks even at 177.4 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.78 against 1.78 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.93 against 1.78 in research, a gap of +0.85.
The best year gives 21% of total P&L (year 3) and calm regimes give 102%; Sharpe is 2.61 in calm and -0.02 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 190 distinct specs; the best of 190 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.56, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.24 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.89 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.48).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.78 to as low as 1.48 (as low as 1.58 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (22 days) give 30% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 19% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Paper trading only: soft test damaging (regime_split EX-6).
